misreadings.quote: The father goes to bed on his own every evening, as soon as the mother asks him, without any help.
misreadings.evidence: "for a quarter of an hour he would remain shaking his head slowly, his eyes closed, without standing up." ... "Only when the two women grabbed him under the armpits would he throw his eyes open" ... "propped up by both women, he would heave himself up"
misreadings.explanation: The father does not go to bed on his own at the mother's first request; he resists for a long time and only rises when both women physically lift him, and he walks alone only for the last stretch after being led to the door.

result.note: Only the reflection version has a clear misreading (the father going to bed unaided at the mother's first request, which the text contradicts and the reflection itself contradicts later); the prose version stays faithful to the passage.
